text: Both slices keep the plan's H, C, I and X rows exactly as stated and name the consumed owner contracts, the consumed event and the outbox and inbox library as facts in the text and in the fakes.
why: The plan fixes the dependency rows of every slice and a worker may not rewrite them, yet the step cannot run without the rwb-litigation event, the rwb-source-data read, the rwb-case answer and the DP-09 library.
read: The consumed AuctionResult event, the three consumed REST rows and RWB-PLT-TE006-CON are named, faked for the build and recorded as missing rows.
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of rwb-litigation, rwb-source-data, rwb-case and the platform library
impact: The story starts on Day 1; the dependency map under-reports four rows until it is corrected

text: The four legacy criteria stay with this story word for word, one shared take-on component serves R-DIS-01, R-DIS-02 and R-DIS-03, the behaviour of R-DIS-01 and R-DIS-02 is proved by RWB-S5-E3019-APP and RWB-S5-E3020-APP, and R-DIS-03 is proved here by one new criterion.
why: The legacy criteria cannot be reworded and three APP stories of the same service carry the same two rule criteria, while the rule of this feature has none.
read: AC1 to AC4 are copied verbatim with their origin tag, AC5 is new and tagged (new, D-RCV-60), and TC-E3-021-02 and TC-E3-021-03 assert the shared component and the contract answers only.
confirm: Business analyst and the S5 service owner, with the owners of RWB-S5-E3019 and RWB-S5-E3020
impact: One implementation of the three take-on routes and no duplicated rule logic; the criterion set of the legacy key is fully owned

text: The LED handover arrives as the AuctionResult event of rwb-litigation on rwb.litigation.events.v1, the LED result, the round and the ladder of 100, 90, 80 then 70 percent are event and decision-record facts, the handover price is written to auction_purchase_price (DF-COL-038) and asset_ref carries the ACE asset key as the only link.
why: Architecture v5 slide 13 makes rwb-asset listen to rwb-litigation and slide 19 IN gives it AuctionResult, while the asset table has no column and no list for the LED facts and no asset_key column.
read: The event property names and the producer story key are carried as placeholders, no table and no column is added, and the ladder and the handed_over result are values of the rule package and of reference data.
confirm: rwb-litigation owner and the solution architect
impact: The step is buildable and testable on Day 1 and no unplanned column or list is created

text: The ACE NPA asset fact is read only on the rwb-source-data DP06 Collateral and assets contract and rwb-asset holds no v_ace_* grant, so the legacy v_ace_npa_asset read is declared as a prohibition.
why: Architecture v5 slides 29, 37 and 45 give the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views to rwb-source-data alone, while the legacy data table of this feature names v_ace_npa_asset and R-PREC puts Architecture v5 above the legacy story.
read: DF-ACE-208 to DF-ACE-219 are P1's and arrive through DP06 Collateral and assets; no v_ace_* path, property or grant is declared and the boundary test fails a build that adds one.
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-source-data owner
impact: No ACE grant is requested for rwb-asset and the asset fact arrives on the owner's contract

text: The case move is the stage outcome answered to rwb-case, with no published REST operation name, and the case state read uses the GET /cases family.
why: No source publishes a case-move operation and the parent CaseWorkflow applies the stage outcome to the case of record.
read: The move answer carries ASSET_ON_BOOKS with the rule ID and version, is faked, and the operation name carries the placeholder.
impact: The step is buildable and testable on Day 1; the name is confirmed before the contract is tagged

text: AssetTakenOn is published from the outbox on rwb.asset.events.v1 and AuctionResult is consumed into the inbox under consumer group rwb-asset-led-handover, both through the platform library RWB-PLT-TE006-CON.
why: Architecture v5 gives the service the topic, the event and two consumers and slide 13 and slide 19 IN give it the consumed events, while the plan's pattern set omits DP-09 and its H row does not carry the library.
read: The published event is the catalogue's event 22, the consumed event is deduplicated by the CloudEvents ID, and the library is recorded as an absent H row rather than added to the metadata.
confirm: Platform library owner and the owners of rwb-litigation, rwb-case and rwb-payment
impact: The events are declared and built with deduplication; a direct publish or a second event fails the absence test

text: The ladder of 100, 90, 80 then 70 percent, the handed_over result, AUCTION_PURCHASE of LOV-TRANSFER-IN and the one-working-day target are read as rule-package and reference-data values and are never written in code.
why: FSD S5 BR-S5-003 and the legacy guardrails forbid a business value in code, and the ladder and the result are not list values of any list in TSD S5 T3.2.
read: The values are named in sections 2, 8 and 13 as values in force at their version and no constant, default or enumeration member of the build carries them.
confirm: Business analyst and the rwb-decision package owner
impact: A change to a percentage or a target is a reference-data or rule-package change and needs no rebuild

text: Both stories stay at Status Draft (realignment v1) and the missing approval of the FSD S5 and the TSD S5 is recorded rather than awaited.
why: The FSD S5 and the TSD S5 are In review with empty sign-off tables and the D-RCV-60 run has no human approval step, and AGENTS.md rule 9 says the work continues in Draft.
read: No source status and no sign-off is changed, the release date 31 January 2027 is copied unchanged and marked tentative, and the verification loop collects the sign-offs later.
applied_in: Metadata row Status of both stories; Sections 3
confirm: Solution architect and the business owner of S5
impact: The stage is not blocked and no approval is claimed that does not exist
